name: How an acceptance criterion is born, built & retired
summary: The data flow of an acceptance criterion through the AC-driven pipeline. A plain-language request is triaged; the product owner and business analyst each write their part into the store and you approve each stage; the IT product owner then records only what each outcome must prove, and its stage passes on its own. A rule check runs after every stage and fails closed, and each passed stage is committed. A deterministic pre-pass gathers file facts, the test designer reads the code and writes the test design and file findings, and that design is committed. Up to two IT product owner hand-back rounds decide undecided file findings, each rule-checked, and a failure stops the run. At the final gate you set one priority; the approval step first reports which criteria are held and why, then approves only the released ones. The scanner then surfaces ready criteria, never one whose test design is pending, a wired ticket is generated, and once its implementation merges the criterion is marked done automatically. Around that spine sit the update paths: scope stays locked to the author, existing code is discovered and back-linked, criteria can be re-homed without breaking references, and retiring one forces its code to be reconciled.

acceptance_scenarios.then: it is classified and checked against the store for duplicates before any AC is authored

acceptance_scenarios.when: the authoring agents for its route run in sequence
acceptance_scenarios.then: L0-L3 acceptance criteria are written to the AC store and never to ticket files, and the IT product owner records per outcome clause whether a test is needed and why, writing no test design

acceptance_scenarios.given: an authoring stage that changed requirement records
acceptance_scenarios.when: the requirement rule check runs at the end of that stage
acceptance_scenarios.then: only one-right-answer violations are repaired, every other finding names its file and rule, and the stage is not complete unless the check passed on at least one record

acceptance_scenarios.given: a rule-checked product owner or business analyst stage
acceptance_scenarios.then: its records are committed to git before the next agent runs, while the IT product owner stage passes its gate automatically and is committed the same way

acceptance_scenarios.given: records carrying test intent and a pre-pass report of their files
acceptance_scenarios.then: each clause that needs a test gets a test design entry grounded in a file it opened and marked with its author, and the file findings are written to a separate field

acceptance_scenarios.given: a test design with a file finding that has no recorded decision
acceptance_scenarios.then: the design is committed, the IT product owner records a decision in at most two rounds, each round is rule-checked as the hand-back stage, and a failed check stops the run before the final gate

acceptance_scenarios.given: a batch in which the hold report holds one record as test design pending
acceptance_scenarios.when: you set priority high and approve
acceptance_scenarios.then: only the released records become approved with that priority and one appended approval entry, the held record stays reviewed and is listed with its reason, and a failed write stops the run before the commit
every todo, unblocked leaf AC is surfaced as prioritized ready work, except one whose test design is still pending

acceptance_scenarios.when: a ticket is generated from it
acceptance_scenarios.then: the ticket is fully wired and the AC records the implemented_by back-reference, and an AC whose test design is pending gets no ticket

acceptance_scenarios.given: an implementing ticket that has merged
acceptance_scenarios.then: the covered ACs' work_status is set to done automatically

acceptance_scenarios.given: an implementation agent editing an AC
acceptance_scenarios.when: it tries to change the criteria text
acceptance_scenarios.then: the change is rejected unless it is the author, and any allowed change is attributed to the agent that made it

acceptance_scenarios.given: an AC whose implementing code already exists
acceptance_scenarios.then: the implementation is matched and linked via covered_by/implemented_by instead of generating a new ticket

acceptance_scenarios.given: an AC referenced from many places
acceptance_scenarios.when: it is moved elsewhere in the tree
acceptance_scenarios.then: its permanent id keeps every existing reference working
leftover code the AC claimed blocks the commit until it is reconciled
